# Flake0 summarize action

Posts one comment per run on the pull request with the [`classify`](../classify/README.md)
verdicts of every failed job:

```
flake0: Integration tests failing due to a mix of test issues and flakiness. Run summary

| Category    | Count | Failing tests                                   |
|-------------|-------|-------------------------------------------------|
| Test issues | 1     | test_build_and_deploy (2 jobs)                  |
| Flaky       | 1     | test_tls_expiration                             |

To fix
- test_build_and_deploy (2 jobs): same empty charm URL error on both arches.
  Recommendation: fix test. Suggested fix: build the charm first.

AI-generated by flake0. It can be wrong, so check before acting on it.
```

Each test name links to its job's summary on the run page. Only charm bugs and test issues get
a line under "To fix".

Rows go worst first: charm bugs (`code_regression`, `code_preexisting`, `workload_defect`),
test issues (`test_defect`), flaky (`environment_infra`, `external_service`, `dependency_drift`),
then no verdict (`INCONCLUSIVE`, `unknown`, or no verdict at all).

Part of the **Flake0** AI debugging suite for CI tests.

## Usage

Each failed job uploads its verdict and updates the comment, so it shows up with the first
failure. One job after all test jobs makes a last model call over all verdicts and the diff. It
groups jobs by test file, can overrule a job's own verdict (the same error on amd64 and arm64 is
not flakiness), and rewrites the comment.

In the test job, after classify:

```yaml
permissions:
  pull-requests: write
steps:
  # ...
  - name: Classify failure
    id: classify
    if: failure()
    uses: canonical/flake0/.github/actions/classify@main
    with: # ...
  - name: Update flake0 PR comment
    if: ${{ failure() && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork }}
    uses: canonical/flake0/.github/actions/summarize@main
    with:
      leg-id: ${{ matrix.name }}  # unique per matrix entry
      job-name: ${{ matrix.name }}
      verdict-path: ${{ steps.classify.outputs.verdict-path }}
      job-id: ${{ job.check_run_id }}  # links each test to this job's summary
```

After all test jobs:

```yaml
flake0-summary:
  needs: [integration-test]
  # cancelled(): a cancelled run would otherwise keep "Run in progress" for good
  if: ${{ (failure() || cancelled()) && github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !github.event.pull_request.head.repo.fork }}
  runs-on: ubuntu-latest
  permissions:
    pull-requests: write
    actions: read  # logs of jobs that classify left without a verdict
  steps:
    - uses: canonical/flake0/.github/actions/summarize@main
      with:
        mode: final
        openrouter-api-key: ${{ secrets.OPENROUTER_API_KEY }}
```

A failed job whose classify step was skipped (it failed before its tests) or failed shows up
under "No verdict" while the run goes on. The final job reads that job's log, which GitHub serves
once the job is done, and classifies it with the rest. Without `actions: read` it stays "No
verdict". If a reusable workflow holds the final job, its callers must grant `actions: read` too.
Green runs, other events and fork pull requests (no secrets, so no verdicts) get no comment. A
re-run attempt gets its own comment. The action never fails the job.

## Inputs

| Input | Default | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `update` | `update` in each failed job, `final` in the job after them |
| `leg-id` | `github.job` | update: unique per matrix entry, used in the artifact name |
| `job-name` | `github.job` | update: job name when classify left no verdict |
| `verdict-path` | `""` | update: the classify step's `verdict-path` output |
| `job-id` | `""` | update: `job.check_run_id`, so the comment links each test to this job's summary |
| `openrouter-api-key` | `""` | final: key for the last call. Empty posts the per-job verdicts. |
| `model` | `z-ai/glm-5.3` | final: OpenRouter model slug |

## Notes

### Concurrent jobs

Two jobs can update the comment at the same moment, and one edit can be lost. Every update
rebuilds the comment from all verdicts uploaded so far, so the next update or the final job
repairs it. If two jobs both post a first comment, the next update deletes the newer one.

### Untrusted text

Verdicts come from model replies to pull request logs. The comment shows them as single lines,
with HTML escaped and `@` mentions broken, and only edits or deletes bot comments that start with
this run's marker. Links, images, `#` references and code span breaks are escaped too.

## Development

```bash
# from the repo root
pytest tests/test_summarize.py
ruff check .github/actions/summarize/scripts/summarize.py
shellcheck -S style .github/actions/summarize/scripts/run.sh

# render a comment from downloaded verdict artifacts
python3 .github/actions/summarize/scripts/summarize.py --verdicts verdicts --run-url URL \
  --marker '<!-- flake0-summary run=1 attempt=1 -->' --out body.md
```
